canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing treats chain-of-thought reasoning as a model capability or process for solving complex problems through sequential intermediate steps before a final answer. Most definitions differ mainly on whether those steps are framed as observable text, such as step-numbered traces or intermediate reasoning before the answer, or as a latent ability that can be elicited by prompting. Smaller lines of work broaden it to procedural or question-decomposition styles of stepwise problem solving, recast it as multi-turn reasoning across interaction turns, or define an internal version in which models decompose composite tasks and process them sequentially across network layers even when no steps are verbalized. A further minority frames it as the ability to benefit from CoT prompting rather than the reasoning process itself, and one paper reports no evidence that explicit CoT prompts improve time series analysis.

Space of facets. Papers use a broad cluster of near-synonyms for the same family of phenomena, including multistep reasoning, multi-step reasoning, chain-of-reasoning, step-by-step thinking, sequential inference, procedural reasoning, and step-wise reasoning. The same family of labels is used both for latent abilities and for observable behaviors, from subtask execution and explicit reasoning traces to broader thinking or planning in natural language. The clearest subtype distinction is between explicit chain generation in token space and internal chain-of-thought, which is presented as task-level decomposition executed layer by layer rather than overt text. Multi-turn formulations add another distinction by treating the construct as sequential decision making over several turns with an external environment.

Space of measurement. Operationalization is dominated by benchmark datasets: papers link the construct to 20 measurement instruments, with GSM8K, 2WikiMultiHopQA, BIG-Bench Hard, and AQuA-RAT among the most frequently linked. These linked instruments are benchmark-style measures rather than human evaluation, LLM-as-a-judge, or probe measures, and many are described as requiring multi-step, multi-hop, or connected reasoning. Papers also link the construct to 13 behavioral indicators, most often chain of thought and several application-oriented behaviors. This benchmark-centered operationalization aligns more directly with the common step-by-step framing than with definitions centered on internal layer-wise or multi-turn reasoning.

Links. Several papers claim causal relationships involving chain of thought and reasoning: papers claim a causal relationship from chain of thought to this construct, from this construct to reasoning, and from planning, reasoning, and visual grounding to this construct. Other papers claim causal relationships from this construct to application behaviors in dialogue, verification, navigation, refinement, and mathematical settings. No correlational links are reported. Related links connect it to chain of thought and hallucination, alongside a broader cluster of decomposition-oriented and domain-specific behaviors.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing treats chain-of-thought reasoning as a model capability or process for solving complex problems through sequential intermediate steps before a final answer. Most definitions differ mainly on whether those steps are framed as observable text, such as step-numbered traces or intermediate reasoning before the answer, or as a latent ability that can be elicited by prompting. Smaller lines of work broaden it to procedural or question-decomposition styles of stepwise problem solving, recast it as multi-turn reasoning across interaction turns, or define an internal version in which models decompose composite tasks and process them sequentially across network layers even when no steps are verbalized. A further minority frames it as the ability to benefit from CoT prompting rather than the reasoning process itself, and one paper reports no evidence that explicit CoT prompts improve time series analysis.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use a broad cluster of near-synonyms for the same family of phenomena, including multistep reasoning, multi-step reasoning, chain-of-reasoning, step-by-step thinking, sequential inference, procedural reasoning, and step-wise reasoning. The same family of labels is used both for latent abilities and for observable behaviors, from subtask execution and explicit reasoning traces to broader thinking or planning in natural language. The clearest subtype distinction is between explicit chain generation in token space and internal chain-of-thought, which is presented as task-level decomposition executed layer by layer rather than overt text. Multi-turn formulations add another distinction by treating the construct as sequential decision making over several turns with an external environment.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Operationalization is dominated by benchmark datasets: papers link the construct to 20 measurement instruments, with GSM8K, 2WikiMultiHopQA, BIG-Bench Hard, and AQuA-RAT among the most frequently linked. These linked instruments are benchmark-style measures rather than human evaluation, LLM-as-a-judge, or probe measures, and many are described as requiring multi-step, multi-hop, or connected reasoning. Papers also link the construct to 13 behavioral indicators, most often chain of thought and several application-oriented behaviors. This benchmark-centered operationalization aligns more directly with the common step-by-step framing than with definitions centered on internal layer-wise or multi-turn reasoning.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Several papers claim causal relationships involving chain of thought and reasoning: papers claim a causal relationship from chain of thought to this construct, from this construct to reasoning, and from planning, reasoning, and visual grounding to this construct. Other papers claim causal relationships from this construct to application behaviors in dialogue, verification, navigation, refinement, and mathematical settings. No correlational links are reported. Related links connect it to chain of thought and hallucination, alongside a broader cluster of decomposition-oriented and domain-specific behaviors.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define chain-of-thought reasoning as multi-step problem solving that decomposes a problem into intermediate inferential steps leading to a final answer, but many differ on whether those steps must be explicitly generated in the output, are a latent internal capability, or occur in interactive or evidence-accumulation settings. These differences mostly describe different aspects or scopes of the same sequential reasoning phenomenon rather than substantially different constructs.
